ai.description: *Ichthyophis moustakius* is a slender caecilian reaching 25–30 cm. It is dark brown with a distinct yellow lateral stripe and a prominent, pale, moustache-like marking on the upper lip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ichthyophis moustakius* is uniquely distinguished by its distinct, cream-colored lateral stripe that extends from the lower jaw to the neck, forming a prominent "moustache."
ai.habitat: *Ichthyophis moustakius* inhabits moist, subtropical broadleaf forests in Manipur, India, typically found in damp soil near streams at altitudes of 800–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Manipur Moustached Ichthyophis is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ichthyophis moustakius* is oviparous, laying clutches of 20–30 eggs in underground burrows near water. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ichthyophis moustakius* is endemic to the state of Manipur in Northeast India, where it inhabits mid-elevation tropical forests within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The *Ichthyophis moustakius* produces a faint, high-pitched, rhythmic clicking or piping sound, typically emitted from within subterranean burrows near forest streams.
